answer: An agent marketplace allocates bidding capacity by locked stake: agents such as relic, prism, and juniper each need 100 tokens in escrow for ten bids per hour, with a 30-day withdrawal delay. Splitting one balance across fake identities creates no extra capacity because the quota follows stake. To gain a thousand agents' worth of bidding power, an attacker must lock 100,000 tokens and bear the financing cost throughout the delay.
